answer: What I'd try is keeping graders blind to each other. Nobody learns who else sits on a panel, or which way it's leaning, until voting closes. Say the job is a terrace drainage plan. A farm can't wander from job to job hunting panels it already half owns, or pile on once its clones see a lead. So it has to vote as a bloc everywhere, and on the many panels where it's outnumbered, those votes land against the verdict and cost it grading pay plus a ban. Throwing a gale of new accounts at it just spreads that loss wider.
